items.title: The Unopened Pack
items.question: A man lies dead in a field with an unopened backpack nearby. No wounds, no footprints around. What failed?
items.correctExplanation: Parachute failed — the backpack held a chute that never deployed: falling explains field, intact pack, solitude. Sky writes sparse reports.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is parachute failed. Unopened pack plus empty field equals skydive gone wrong: no wounds needed when gravity obliges. Backpacks sometimes hold last chances.
items.lessonContent:
Backpacks sometimes hold last chances.
Empty fields plus intact packs speak.
Gravity obliges without wounding ever.
Sky writes sparse reports always.
Share this: pack one backup today.

items.title: The Bicycle Hand
items.question: A man lies dead clutching cards, surrounded by 53 bicycles. Police close the case within the hour. What happened?

items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is cheating at cards. Bicycles here are playing cards, fifty-three of them: caught with extras, punished promptly. Brands name murder weapons sometimes.
items.lessonContent:

Decks deal death rarely but finally.

items.title: The Slow Sipper
items.question: Two men drink identical poisoned cocktails; the fast drinker lives, the slow one dies. What differed?
items.correctExplanation: Melted ice — poison frozen in cubes: fast glasses finished before melting, slow sipped death. Speed beat chemistry once.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is melted ice. Identical pours, different paces: cubes held poison hostage until melt. Slow sipping freed what fast drinking dodged.
items.lessonContent:
Paces decide poisonings sometimes.
Cubes hold death hostage temporarily.
Identical pours diverge by speed.
Slow sips free frozen fates.

items.title: The Darkroom Alibi
items.question: A woman shoots her husband, holds him underwater for five minutes, then hangs him — and walks free with his blessing. What was her evening?

items.incorrectExplanation: Actually, the answer is photo development. Shoot, submerge, hang: photography's vocabulary mimics murder's. Blessing follows when subjects understand mediums.
items.lessonContent:

Verbs mislead without contexts attached.
Mediums explain apparent murders.
Blessings follow understood processes.

items.title: The Last Supper
items.question: A man orders turtle soup, takes one spoonful, pays, walks out, and ends his life. The broth told him something unbearable. What?

items.title: The Halved Match

items.title: The Drowning Verdict
items.question: Condemned, told 'one true statement hangs you, one false drowns you' — he walks free. What did he say?
items.correctExplanation: Drown me — true means hanging (contradicting the statement), false means drowning (fulfilling it): paradox paralyzes executioners. Verdicts tangle gallows.
items.incorrectExplanation: Not quite — the answer is drown me. Hanging a truth-teller breaks the rules; drowning a liar fulfills them: both options self-defeat. Self-reference frees the condemned.
items.lessonContent:

True hangs, false drowns — except this.
